title: Who is wise, who is rich
hookLine: who is wise? one who learns from everyone; who is rich? one content with their portion (Pirkei Avot 4:1)
tomorrow: if the whole earth full of wealth were yours, would it save you?

lines: ONE WHO LEARNS FROM EVERY PERSON.
cards: Quiz shows crown whoever knows the most. Ben Zoma, a sage in Pirkei Avot, ran a different quiz. Who is wise?
One who learns from every person. Who is mighty? One who masters their own impulse.
Who is rich? One who is glad with their portion. Who is honored?
One who honors others. Four questions, and every answer turns the prize inside out. Wisdom isn't what you've stored up; it's who you're willing to learn from.

teach.b: The Talmud shows Ben Zoma living it. He stood on a step on the Temple Mount and looked at the crowd, and said: blessed is the one who created all these to serve me. That sounds proud until he explains.
Think how hard the first human worked for bread: plowing, sowing, reaping, threshing, grinding, kneading, baking. And I wake up and find it ready.

teach.h: ALL THE TRADES COME TO MY DOOR.
teach.b: All the trades come to my door. So the crowd wasn't a nuisance to him. It was a room full of people whose work fed and clothed him, every one with something to teach.
The same page of the Talmud gives a blessing for seeing a great crowd of Israel: blessed is the one who knows the secrets, because no two minds in it are alike.
That's the teaching. In Judaism even a crowd gets a blessing, and wisdom starts by noticing who you owe.

how: Jews study Ben Zoma's four questions in Pirkei Avot, and a traditional blessing is said on seeing a great crowd of Jews, praising God who knows the secrets of every heart.

o: one who has read the most holy books
one who learns from every person they meet
one who keeps quiet and never asks for help

games.q: Ben Zoma's four questions: tap the pairs.
p: one who learns from every person

s: in Pirkei Avot, the wise one is the person who knows the most
Ben Zoma: the wise one learns from every person.
Ben Zoma blessed the crowd because all the trades came to his door
in the Talmud he counts the work behind bread and clothes, and finds it all ready for him.
Ben Zoma's blessing on the crowd was a boast that people exist to serve him
he explains it as gratitude: think how hard the first human worked for bread, and I find it ready.

games.q: your new coworker is younger, louder and keeps doing things 'wrong.' Ben Zoma's way, what's the wise move?
o: ask what she knows that you don't; the wise learn from every person.
keep your head down; wisdom is knowing more than the people around you.
teach her the right way first; you can learn from her later.
games.why: Ben Zoma's wise one is the student of everyone, the loud new coworker included.

practice: Take one thing near you, a cup, a shirt, a piece of bread, and count, on your fingers, the hands it passed through to reach you: the grower, the maker, the driver, the shelf stocker.
Pick one of them, and ask what their work could teach you.

wordCard.voice: Who is wise: Ben Zoma's question, and his answer, one who learns from every person.

orig.note: Hebrew, Pirkei Avot 4:1: who is wise? one who learns from every person.

carryVoice: Keep this one: learn from everyone, the crowd included. Six sayings, one whole week, done.

sources.ref: Pirkei Avot 4:1 (Ben Zoma: who is wise, mighty, rich, honored)
Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 58a (Ben Zoma on a step of the Temple Mount; the work behind bread and clothing; the blessing on seeing crowds, 'who knows the secrets')
